Acid Fog.description: This spell conjures a rolling cloud of corrosive mist that functions similarly to a solid fog effect. Beyond impeding movement and blocking vision, the acidic vapors inflict 2d6 points of acid damage each round on your turn to every creature and object caught within the fog, beginning the round you cast it. Arcane Material Component: A pinch of dried, powdered peas mixed with powdered animal hoof.

Acid Splash.description: You launch a small globule of acid toward a target. A successful ranged touch attack is required to strike. The globule inflicts 1d3 points of acid damage on impact.

Aid.description: The recipient receives a +1 morale bonus on attack rolls and saving throws against fear effects, along with temporary hit points equal to 1d8 + caster level (to a maximum of 1d8+10 at caster level 10th).

Air Walk.description: The target gains the ability to walk on air as though it were solid ground. Ascending works like climbing a slope, with a maximum incline of 45 degrees at half the walker's normal movement rate. Winds of 21+ mph can push the subject, displacing it 5 feet per 5 mph of wind speed at the end of each turn. At the GM's discretion, exceptionally powerful or turbulent winds may impose further penalties such as loss of movement control or physical harm. When the spell expires while the subject remains airborne, it descends gradually at 60 feet per round for 1d6 rounds. If it reaches the ground within that time, it lands without injury. Otherwise, it falls the remaining distance, suffering 1d6 points of damage per 10 feet fallen. Dispelling the effect also causes this gradual descent, though an antimagic field does not. You may cast this on a trained mount to ride it through the air. Training a mount for air walking takes one week of effort and a DC 25 Handle Animal check.

Alarm.description: This spell sets a ward that triggers a mental or audible alert whenever a creature of Tiny size or larger enters or touches the protected area. A creature that speaks a password you set during casting does not activate the alarm. You choose the alarm type at the time of casting. Mental Alarm: Only you are alerted, as long as you remain within 1 mile of the area. You perceive a single mental signal that can wake you from normal sleep but otherwise does not break concentration. Silence effects cannot suppress a mental alarm. Audible Alarm: The alarm produces the sound of a small bell, audible within 60 feet. Closed doors reduce this range by 10 feet each, and substantial walls reduce it by 20 feet. Under quiet conditions, the sound can be faintly heard up to 180 feet away. It lasts for 1 round. Creatures inside a silence effect cannot hear it. Ethereal and astral creatures do not set off the alarm. This spell can be made permanent with a permanency spell. Arcane Focus: A miniature bell and a length of fine silver wire.

Align Weapon.description: You imbue a weapon with a chosen alignment: good, evil, lawful, or chaotic. An aligned weapon can overcome the damage reduction of certain creatures, typically outsiders of the opposing alignment. This has no effect on weapons that already possess an alignment. Natural weapons such as unarmed strikes cannot be affected. The spell itself takes on the alignment descriptor matching the alignment you bestow.

Alter Self.description: You change your physical form to that of another creature sharing your type (such as humanoid or magical beast). The new form must be within one size category of your normal size, and its maximum HD equals your caster level (up to 5 HD at 5th level). You may assume the appearance of your own species or even your own likeness. You keep your own ability scores, class features, level, hit points, alignment, base attack bonus, and base saves. All supernatural and spell-like attacks and qualities of your original form are retained unless they require a body part the new form lacks. Class-derived extraordinary abilities persist, but extraordinary abilities from your natural form that are not class-based are lost. If the new form can speak, you communicate normally. You retain spellcasting, but the new form must be capable of intelligible speech for verbal components and must have hands capable of fine manipulation for somatic or material components. You gain the new form's physical characteristics while keeping your own mind. Physical qualities include natural size, mundane movement modes (burrowing, climbing, walking, swimming, and flight up to 120 feet or 60 feet for non-flying movement), natural armor bonus, natural weapons, racial skill bonuses, racial bonus feats, and gross physical features like the number of limbs. Extra limbs do not grant additional attacks. You do not acquire extraordinary special attacks or qualities beyond those listed, such as darkvision, blindsense, fast healing, regeneration, or scent. Supernatural abilities and spell-like abilities of the new form are not gained. Your creature type and subtype remain the same, and you cannot assume the form of any templated creature. You control the new form's minor and significant physical details within normal ranges for its kind. You are effectively disguised as a typical member of the new form's race, gaining a +10 bonus on Disguise checks. Equipment either remains worn or held by the new form if possible, or melds into it and becomes nonfunctional. On reverting, melded items reappear in their original positions and become functional again. Items worn in the assumed form that cannot be worn in your true form fall at your feet. Items held in body parts common to both forms remain held. Any separated body part or equipment piece reverts to its true form.

Analyze Dweomer.description: You perceive all active spells and magical properties on creatures or objects you examine. Each round, as a free action, you may scrutinize one visible creature or object. For magic items, you learn their functions, activation methods, and remaining charges if applicable. For objects or creatures with active spells, you identify each spell, its effect, and its caster level. An attended object may attempt a Will save if its holder desires; success means you learn nothing beyond what is visually apparent. An object that saves cannot be affected by this spell again for 24 hours. This spell does not function on artifacts. Focus: A tiny lens of ruby or sapphire set in a small golden loop worth at least 1,500 gp.

Animal Growth.description: Multiple animals double in height and increase to eight times their normal weight. Each animal advances one size category (for instance, from Large to Huge), gaining a +8 size bonus to Strength, a +4 size bonus to Constitution (and thus 2 extra hit points per HD), and taking a -2 size penalty to Dexterity. Natural armor improves by 2. The size change modifies each animal's AC, attack rolls, and base damage appropriately. Space and reach adjust according to the new size, but speed remains unchanged. Each subject also gains damage reduction 10/magic and a +4 resistance bonus on saving throws. If there is not enough room for the full growth, the creature grows as large as the space allows and may attempt a Strength check (using increased Strength) to burst any enclosure. Failure means it is harmlessly constrained. The spell does not enlarge equipment magically (enlarged gear returns to normal size if it leaves the creature's possession), and it grants no control over the affected animals. Multiple size-increasing magical effects do not stack.

Animal Messenger.description: You compel a Tiny animal to travel to a location you specify. The creature cannot be one already tamed or trained by another, including familiars and animal companions. You lure it with appropriate food, and it approaches to await instructions. You mentally imprint a well-known place or obvious landmark as the destination. The directions must be simple since the animal relies on your knowledge. You may attach a small item or note to it. The animal travels to the location and waits until the spell expires, then resumes its natural behavior. While waiting, it allows others to approach and remove any attached scroll or token. Recipients gain no special ability to communicate with the animal or read any attached message in an unfamiliar language. Material Component: A morsel of food the animal finds appealing.

Animal Shapes.description: This functions like polymorph, except you transform up to one willing creature per caster level into an animal form of your choosing. Unwilling creatures are unaffected. All recipients must assume the same type of animal. Recipients remain transformed until the spell expires or you dismiss it for all subjects. An individual subject may use a full-round action to resume its normal form, ending the spell for that subject only. The maximum HD of the assumed form is the lesser of the subject's HD or your caster level, up to 20 HD at 20th level.

Animal Trance.description: Your rhythmic movements and music (or singing or chanting) compel animals and magical beasts to simply watch you. Only creatures with an Intelligence score of 1 or 2 can be affected. Roll 2d6 to determine the total HD of creatures you fascinate, affecting the closest targets first. A magical beast, dire animal, or attack/guard-trained animal is entitled to a saving throw; untrained animals are not.

Animate Dead.description: You transform corpses or skeletal remains into undead skeletons or zombies that obey your verbal commands. They can follow you, guard an area, or attack creatures entering a designated location. They persist until destroyed (and cannot be re-animated once destroyed). A single casting cannot create more undead HD than twice your caster level. You control the created undead indefinitely, but you can control no more than 4 HD of undead per caster level total. Exceeding this limit means newly created undead fall under your control while excess undead from previous castings become uncontrolled (you choose which to release). Cleric command/rebuke undead do not count against this limit. Skeletons require a mostly intact corpse or skeleton with bones. Zombies require a mostly intact corpse with a true anatomy. Statistics depend on size, not the creature's living abilities. Material Component: A black onyx gem worth at least 25 gp per HD of undead, placed in the mouth or eye socket of each corpse. The spell consumes the gems, leaving worthless shells.

Animate Objects.description: You grant inanimate objects mobility and a semblance of life. Each animated object immediately attacks whatever target you designate. Any nonmagical material can be animated. You may animate one Small or smaller object per caster level, with larger objects counting as multiples: Medium counts as 2, Large as 4, Huge as 8, Gargantuan as 16, and Colossal as 32. You can redirect targets as a move action. Objects carried or worn by creatures cannot be animated. This effect can be made permanent with a permanency spell.

Animate Plants.description: You grant inanimate plants mobility and a semblance of life. Each animated plant immediately attacks your designated targets as an animated object of the corresponding size. You may animate one Large or smaller plant per three caster levels, with larger plants counting as multiples: Huge counts as 2, Gargantuan as 4, and Colossal as 8. You can change targets as a move action. Plants smaller than Large lack hardness unless the GM rules otherwise. This spell cannot affect plant creatures or nonliving vegetable material. Alternatively, you may imbue all plants within range with mobility to entangle nearby creatures, duplicating the entangle spell. Spell resistance does not prevent entanglement. This alternate effect lasts 1 hour per caster level.

Animate Rope.description: You animate a nonliving ropelike object such as string, yarn, cord, line, rope, or cable. The maximum length assumes a 1-inch diameter rope. Each additional inch of thickness reduces the maximum length by 50%, while each halving of diameter increases it by 50%. Available commands include coil, coil and knot, loop, loop and knot, tie and knot, and their opposites. You issue one command per round as a move action. The rope can only ensnare a creature or object within 1 foot of it and must be thrown near the target (requiring a ranged touch attack with a 10-foot range increment). A standard 1-inch hempen rope has 2 hp, AC 10, and requires a DC 23 Strength check to burst. It deals no damage but can serve as a trip line or entangle a creature that fails a Reflex save. A bound spellcaster must succeed on a DC 15 Concentration check to cast. An entangled creature can escape with a DC 20 Escape Artist check. The rope and its knots are mundane. You gain a +2 bonus on Use Rope checks with the affected rope. Objects carried or worn by creatures cannot be animated.

Antilife Shell.description: You create a mobile, hemispherical barrier of energy that excludes most living creatures. Animals, aberrations, dragons, fey, giants, humanoids, magical beasts, monstrous humanoids, oozes, plants, and vermin cannot enter, though constructs, elementals, outsiders, and undead are unaffected. This spell can only be used defensively; forcing the barrier against excluded creatures collapses it.

Antimagic Field.description: An invisible barrier moves with you, rendering the enclosed space impervious to most magical effects, spell-like abilities, supernatural abilities, and magic items. The field suppresses but does not dispel magic within it or brought into it. For example, a hasted creature loses the benefit inside but regains it upon leaving. Time in the field counts against suppressed durations. Summoned creatures and incorporeal undead wink out upon entering, reappearing when the field departs; time spent winked out counts against their duration. If a summoned creature has spell resistance, you must succeed on a caster level check (1d20 + caster level) against it. Instantaneous conjuration results are unaffected. Normal creatures and mundane missiles can enter freely. A magical sword loses its magical properties but remains a masterwork weapon. Golems and constructs imbued with magic during creation are unaffected unless summoned. Non-summoned elementals, corporeal undead, and outsiders are likewise unaffected, though their spell-like and supernatural abilities may be temporarily suppressed. Dispel magic cannot remove the field. Overlapping antimagic fields have no effect on each other. Certain spells like wall of force, prismatic sphere, and prismatic wall remain unaffected. Artifacts and deities are immune. A creature larger than the field is only affected in the portion within the barrier. Arcane Material Component: A pinch of powdered iron or iron filings.

Antipathy.description: You cause an object or location to radiate magical vibrations that repel a specific named kind of intelligent creature or a specific named alignment. The creature kind must be precise (not a subtype), and the alignment must be exact. Designated creatures feel an overwhelming compulsion to leave the area or avoid the item, never willingly returning while the spell lasts. A successful saving throw allows a creature to remain, but it suffers a -4 Dexterity penalty from the distracting discomfort. This spell counters and dispels sympathy. Arcane Material Component: A lump of alum soaked in vinegar.

Antiplant Shell.description: You create an invisible, mobile barrier that shields all creatures inside from attacks by plant creatures and animated plants. As with similar abjurations, forcing the barrier against creatures it excludes causes the field to collapse.

Arcane Eye.description: You create an invisible magical sensor that transmits visual information to you. You can place it at any visible point, after which it can travel beyond your line of sight. It moves at 30 feet per round when scanning primarily at floor level, or 10 feet per round when also examining walls and ceilings. It sees exactly as you would. It can travel in any direction for the spell's duration. Solid barriers block it, but it can pass through openings as small as 1 inch. It cannot cross planar boundaries. You must concentrate to use it; otherwise it remains inert. Material Component: A bit of bat fur.

Arcane Lock.description: You magically seal a door, chest, or portal. You can pass through your own arcane lock freely. Others can open the sealed object only by breaking in, or with a successful dispel magic or knock spell. The normal DC to force open the affected object increases by 10. A knock spell suppresses the arcane lock for 10 minutes without removing it. Material Component: Gold dust worth 25 gp.

Arcane Mark.description: You inscribe a personal rune or mark of up to six characters on any substance, even stone or metal, without damaging the material. The mark can be visible or invisible. An invisible mark glows when detect magic is cast but is not necessarily legible. See invisibility, true seeing, a gem of seeing, or a robe of eyes also reveals an invisible mark. Read magic reveals any words in the mark. The mark cannot be dispelled but can be removed by the caster or an erase spell. On a living being, the mark fades naturally in about a month. Arcane mark must be placed on an object before casting instant summons on that same object.

Arcane Sight.description: Your eyes glow blue, granting you the ability to perceive magical auras within 120 feet. Unlike detect magic, this requires no concentration and reveals aura locations and strength more quickly. You can make Spellcraft checks (DC 15 + spell level, or 15 + half caster level for non-spell effects) to identify the school of magic for each aura in line of sight. By concentrating on a specific creature within 120 feet as a standard action, you can determine whether it possesses spellcasting or spell-like abilities, whether they are arcane or divine, and the strength of its most powerful available spell or spell-like ability. Results may appear deceptively low for casters who have expended most of their daily allotment. This spell can be made permanent with permanency.

Arcane Sight, Greater.description: This functions like arcane sight, except you automatically identify which spells or magical effects are active on any individual or object you observe. It does not identify magic items. Unlike arcane sight, this version cannot be made permanent with permanency.

Astral Projection.description: You free your spirit from your body and project an astral form onto another plane. Willing creatures linked in a circle with you at the time of casting can accompany you as dependent travelers. Your physical body remains on the Material Plane in suspended animation. An astral copy of you and your equipment appears on the Astral Plane. From there, you can travel to other planes by leaving the Astral Plane and forming a new physical body and equipment on the destination plane. A silvery cord connects your astral and physical forms; severing it kills you. When a second body is formed, the cord attaches invisibly to it. If the second body or astral form is slain, the cord returns you to your Material Plane body, reviving it. Astral projections function on the Astral Plane but must materialize physical bodies to affect other planes. Travel is indefinite until you choose to end it or it is terminated by outside means such as dispel magic on either form, cord destruction, or destruction of your physical body. Material Component: A jacinth worth at least 1,000 gp, plus a silver bar worth 5 gp per person affected.

Atonement.description: This spell lifts the burden of misdeeds from a truly repentant creature. If the wrongdoing was unwitting or coerced, the spell works at no cost. For deliberate, knowing transgressions, you must intercede with your deity (expending 500 XP). Many casters first assign a quest or similar penance to verify sincerity. The spell has several applications: Reverse Magical Alignment Change restores an alignment altered by magic at no XP cost. Restore Class can return a fallen paladin's class features. Restore Cleric or Druid Spell Powers can be granted by another cleric of the same deity or another druid (costing 500 XP if the transgression was intentional). Redemption or Temptation allows you to offer a creature of opposing alignment the chance to voluntarily change its alignment to match yours; no compulsion can force acceptance, and this does not work on outsiders or creatures incapable of natural alignment change. The spell applies equally to acts against any alignment, not just evil. Material Component: Burning incense. Focus: A set of prayer beads or similar prayer device worth at least 500 gp. XP Cost: 500 XP per casting when the guilt was from deliberate acts.

Augury.description: You gain insight into whether a specific contemplated action will yield good or bad results in the near future. The base chance for a meaningful answer is 70% + 1% per caster level (maximum 90%), rolled secretly by the GM. The result is one of four outcomes: weal, woe, weal and woe, or nothing. A failed roll also produces "nothing," with no way to distinguish between the two. The spell foresees only about 30 minutes ahead, so long-term consequences may not factor in. Repeated auguries by the same person on the same topic reuse the initial result. Material Component: Incense worth at least 25 gp. Focus: A set of marked sticks, bones, or similar tokens worth at least 25 gp.

Awaken.description: You grant humanlike sentience to a tree or animal. You must succeed on a Will save (DC 10 + the creature's current HD, or the HD the tree will gain). The awakened creature is friendly toward you but has no special empathic connection; it will serve you in specific tasks if you communicate your wishes. An awakened tree gains animated object characteristics with the plant type, and each of its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores become 3d6. An awakened animal gains 3d6 Intelligence, +1d3 Charisma, and +2 HD, with its type becoming magical beast (augmented animal). An awakened animal cannot serve as a companion, familiar, or special mount. The awakened creature speaks one language you know, plus additional languages equal to its Intelligence bonus. XP Cost: 250 XP.

Baleful Polymorph.description: You transform the target into a Small or smaller animal of no more than 1 HD. The subject adopts all statistics and special abilities of the new form's average member, except it retains its own class features and loses all special abilities from its original form. All items fall to the ground. If the new form would be fatal (such as a fish on land), the target gains a +4 bonus on the save. If the subject remains transformed for 24 consecutive hours, it must attempt a Will save; failure causes it to lose all memories and language comprehension, with its HD and hp adjusting to match the new form (reversible if the effect later ends). Incorporeal or gaseous creatures are immune, and shapechanger creatures can revert to their natural form as a standard action, ending the spell.

Bane.description: Your enemies become filled with doubt and dread. Each affected creature suffers a -1 penalty on attack rolls and a -1 penalty on saving throws against fear effects. Bane counters and dispels bless.

Banishment.description: A more potent version of dismissal, this spell forces extraplanar creatures out of your home plane. You can banish up to 2 HD of creatures per caster level. Presenting objects or substances the target hates, fears, or opposes grants a +1 bonus per item on your caster level check to overcome spell resistance, and increases the save DC by 2 per item. At the GM's option, certain rare items may provide double the normal bonuses. Arcane Focus: Any item distasteful to the subject (optional).

Barkskin.description: The target's skin toughens, granting a +2 enhancement bonus to its existing natural armor bonus. This bonus increases by 1 for every three caster levels above 3rd, to a maximum of +5 at 12th level. This enhancement stacks with natural armor but not with other enhancement bonuses to natural armor. A creature without natural armor effectively has a +0 natural armor bonus.

Bear's Endurance.description: The target gains enhanced vitality and stamina through a +4 enhancement bonus to Constitution, providing the usual benefits to hit points, Fortitude saves, and Constitution checks. Hit points gained this way are not temporary hit points; they vanish when Constitution returns to normal and are not lost first.

Bear's Endurance, Mass.description: This functions like bear's endurance, except it affects multiple creatures.

Bestow Curse.description: You afflict the target with a curse, choosing from one of three effects. The curse cannot be dispelled, but it can be removed by break enchantment, limited wish, miracle, remove curse, or wish. This spell counters remove curse.

Bigby's Clenched Fist.description: A Large floating hand appears and attacks a target you designate. The hand strikes once per round on your turn with an attack bonus equal to your caster level + your relevant ability modifier + 11 (for its Strength and size). It deals 1d8+11 points of damage on each hit and can also attempt a bull rush with a bonus of +15, pushing the target back without provoking opportunity attacks. Directing the hand to a new target is a move action. The hand has as many hit points as you have at full health, has your save bonuses, and has an AC of 20 (-1 size, +11 natural). It takes half damage from energy attacks but full damage from physical attacks.

Bigby's Crushing Hand.description: This creates a Large hand that can both interpose itself defensively and crush opponents. The hand provides cover (+4 AC bonus) when interposing and can grapple. Its grapple bonus equals your caster level + your relevant ability modifier + 12 (Strength plus size). A successfully grappled foe takes 2d6+12 points of damage each round. The hand can also bull rush at +18. You direct its actions as a move action.

Bigby's Forceful Hand.description: A Large hand of force appears, interposing itself between you and a chosen opponent to provide cover. The hand moves to stay between you and the target, giving you a +4 AC bonus. It can also bull rush with a +14 bonus without provoking opportunity attacks. The hand always moves with you, remaining between you and the designated foe. Directing it to a new target is a move action.

Bigby's Grasping Hand.description: A Large hand appears that can interpose defensively or grapple. It provides cover (+4 AC bonus) when interposing and can initiate grapples with a bonus equal to your caster level + your relevant ability modifier + 10 (for its Strength and size). A grappled target takes 2d6+10 points of damage per round. You can redirect the hand to a new target as a move action.

Bigby's Interposing Hand.description: A Large hand of force appears between you and one opponent you designate. The hand moves to remain between you and the target, providing cover that grants a +4 bonus to AC against that foe. A creature trying to push past it must overcome the hand in an opposed check using its Strength modifier against the hand's bonus (your caster level + your relevant ability modifier). The hand does not prevent spells or ranged attacks. You can redirect it to a new target as a move action. The hand has hp equal to half your full hp, your save bonuses, and an AC of 20.

Binding.description: This spell creates a magical restraint to hold a creature. You must have precise knowledge of the creature's identity. The target receives a Will save, modified by -1 for each binding of the same type currently maintained on other creatures. Several versions exist, from simple chains that immobilize the target to more elaborate prisons including minimus containment (shrinking the target into a gem), slumber (enchanted sleep), and bound slumber (chained and asleep). Higher versions require higher-level spells and may need additional material components. A bound creature may attempt escape at intervals depending on the version used. Material components and focuses vary by version, with the base requiring a continuous chanting and special materials worth at least 500 gp.

Blade Barrier.description: A vertical wall of whirling blades made of force springs into being. Any creature passing through takes 1d6 points of damage per caster level (maximum 15d6), with a Reflex save for half. The wall provides cover. Creatures forced through the barrier by others take full damage with no save. The barrier is immobile once created. If you evoke the barrier where creatures stand, each takes damage as if passing through.

Blasphemy.description: Any nongood creature within the area suffers cumulative, concurrent effects based on its HD relative to your caster level, with no saving throw. These effects include: deafened for 1d4 rounds, dazed for 1 round, weakened (with 2d4 points of Strength damage), and potentially paralyzed for 1d10 minutes. Nongood extraplanar creatures on your home plane are instantly banished and cannot return for at least 24 hours; the banishment allows a Will save at -4. Creatures whose HD exceed your caster level are unaffected.

Bless.description: You fill your allies with courage. Each ally gains a +1 morale bonus on attack rolls and a +1 morale bonus on saving throws against fear effects. Bless counters and dispels bane.

Bless Water.description: This spell imbues a flask (1 pint) of water with positive energy, transforming it into holy water. Holy water damages undead and evil outsiders. Material Component: 5 pounds of powdered silver (worth 25 gp).

Bless Weapon.description: This spell makes a weapon strike true against evil foes. The weapon is treated as having a +1 enhancement bonus for overcoming the damage reduction of evil creatures, though this does not modify attack or damage rolls. It also counts as good-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. In addition, all critical hit rolls against evil foes are automatically confirmed. This spell can affect up to fifty projectiles at once, with each losing the effect after being used.

Blight.description: You wither a single plant, dealing 1d6 points of damage per level (maximum 15d6). A plant creature or an animated plant can attempt a Fortitude save for half damage. This spell has no effect on creatures that are not plants or plant creatures.

Blindness/Deafness.description: You call upon the powers of unlife to render the target permanently blind or deaf (your choice).

Blink.description: You rapidly and randomly shift between the Material Plane and the Ethereal Plane. While blinking, you gain several benefits: physical attacks against you have a 50% miss chance, and you gain a +2 bonus on attack rolls against non-ethereal opponents (who are considered flat-footed to you). You can strike ethereal creatures as if they were material. Your own physical attacks have a 20% miss chance against material targets since you sometimes blink away during the attack. Individually targeted spells have a 50% chance of failing against you. Area effects originating on the Material Plane affect you at 50% effectiveness. You take half damage from falling while blinking. While ethereal, you can move through solid objects; if you become material inside an object, you are shunted to the nearest open space and take 1d6 damage per 5 feet displaced.

Blur.description: The target's outline shifts and wavers, granting 20% concealment (20% miss chance). See invisibility does not counter blur, but true seeing does. Creatures that cannot see the subject are unaffected.

Break Enchantment.description: You free victims from enchantments, transmutations, and curses, even reversing instantaneous effects like flesh to stone. For each effect, you make a caster level check (1d20 + caster level, maximum +15) against DC 11 + the effect's caster level. Success removes the effect. For cursed magic items, the DC is 25. This spell works against effects that dispel magic cannot handle, provided those effects are 5th level or lower. It does not remove curses from items themselves, but frees the victim from the item's effects.

Bull's Strength.description: The target becomes stronger, gaining a +4 enhancement bonus to Strength with the usual benefits to melee attack rolls, damage rolls, and Strength-based checks. Arcane Material Component: A few hairs or a pinch of dung from a bull.

Bull's Strength, Mass.description: This functions like bull's strength, except it affects multiple creatures.

Burning Hands.description: A cone of searing flame shoots from your fingertips, dealing 1d4 points of fire damage per caster level (maximum 5d4) to every creature in the area. Flammable materials like cloth, paper, and thin wood ignite. A character can extinguish burning items as a full-round action.

Call Lightning.description: Upon completing the spell, and once per round thereafter, you may call down a 5-foot-wide, 30-foot-long vertical bolt of lightning that deals 3d6 points of electricity damage. The bolt strikes wherever you choose within range. You need not call a bolt immediately; on subsequent rounds, doing so requires a standard action. You can call up to one bolt per caster level (maximum 10). Outdoors in stormy conditions (rain, clouds, wind, hot and cloudy, or tornado), each bolt deals 3d10 instead. This spell works indoors and underground but not underwater.

Call Lightning Storm.description: This functions like call lightning, except each bolt deals 5d6 points of electricity damage (or 5d10 in outdoor stormy conditions), and you may call up to 15 bolts.

Calm Animals.description: You soothe animals, rendering them docile and harmless. Only ordinary animals (Intelligence 1 or 2) are eligible, and all must be of the same kind within 30 feet of each other. You can affect up to 2d4 + caster level HD of animals. Dire animals and those trained to attack or guard receive a saving throw; others do not. Calmed animals remain in place without attacking or fleeing, defend themselves if attacked, and break free if threatened by fire, predators, or imminent attack.

Calm Emotions.description: You pacify agitated creatures. Affected creatures cannot take violent actions (though they can defend themselves) or act destructively. Any aggressive action against a calmed creature immediately ends the spell for all subjects. This spell automatically suppresses (but does not dispel) morale bonuses from spells like bless, good hope, and rage, as well as bardic courage inspiration and barbarian rage. It also suppresses fear effects and removes the confused condition. Suppressed effects resume when calm emotions ends, provided their durations have not expired.

Cat's Grace.description: The target becomes more agile and coordinated, gaining a +4 enhancement bonus to Dexterity with the usual benefits to AC, Reflex saves, and Dexterity-based checks. Material Component: A pinch of cat fur.

Cat's Grace, Mass.description: This functions like cat's grace, except it affects multiple creatures.

Cause Fear.description: The target becomes frightened. On a successful Will save, it is only shaken for 1 round. Creatures with 6 or more HD are immune. This spell counters and dispels remove fear.

Chain Lightning.description: An electrical discharge leaps from your fingertips, striking one primary target for 1d6 points of electricity damage per caster level (maximum 20d6). The bolt then arcs to secondary targets up to your caster level in number (maximum 20), each within 30 feet of the primary target, dealing half the primary bolt's damage. No target can be struck more than once, and you choose the secondary targets. Each target may attempt a Reflex save for half damage. Focus: A bit of fur; a piece of amber, glass, or crystal rod; plus one silver pin per caster level.

Changestaff.description: You transform a specially prepared quarterstaff into a Huge treant-like creature approximately 24 feet tall. The staff-creature fights and defends you, obeying spoken commands, but cannot converse with actual treants or control trees. If reduced to 0 or fewer hit points, it crumbles and the staff is destroyed. Otherwise, the staff returns to normal when the spell expires or is dismissed, and can be reused. The creature is always at full strength when created. Focus: A specially prepared quarterstaff carved from a sound ash, oak, or yew limb, requiring twenty-eight days of curing, shaping, and polishing with no strenuous activity.

Chaos Hammer.description: You unleash chaotic energy in a multicolored explosion. Only lawful and neutral creatures take harm. Lawful creatures take 1d8 points of damage per two caster levels (maximum 5d8), or 1d6 per caster level (maximum 10d6) for lawful outsiders, and are slowed for 1d6 rounds. A Will save halves the damage and negates the slow. Neutral creatures take only half damage and are not slowed, and can further halve the damage with a Will save.

Charm Animal.description: This functions like charm person, except it affects a creature of the animal type.

Charm Monster.description: This functions like charm person, except the effect is not restricted by creature type or size.

Charm Monster, Mass.description: This functions like charm monster, except it affects multiple creatures whose combined HD do not exceed twice your level (minimum one creature). If there are more potential targets than you can affect, you choose them one at a time until selecting one with too many HD.

Charm Person.description: You cause a humanoid to regard you as a trusted friend and ally. Creatures currently threatened or attacked by you or your allies get a +5 bonus on the saving throw. You cannot control the charmed person like an automaton, but it interprets your words and actions favorably. Convincing it to do something it would not normally do requires an opposed Charisma check (no retries). It never obeys suicidal or obviously harmful orders, but might be convinced of urgent necessity. Any threatening act by you or your apparent allies ends the spell. You must speak the subject's language or communicate through pantomime.

Chill Metal.description: You make metal extremely cold. Nonmagical, unattended metal gets no save. Magical metal and items in a creature's possession use the higher save bonus. A creature takes cold damage based on its contact with the chilled metal: full damage if wearing affected armor or carrying metal weighing at least one-fifth its weight, minimum damage otherwise. The spell progresses over rounds: no damage on rounds 1 and 7, moderate pain on rounds 2 and 6, and freezing cold on rounds 3 through 5. Heat damage offsets cold damage point-for-point. Underwater, the spell deals no damage but forms ice around the metal. This spell counters and dispels heat metal.

Chill Touch.description: Your hand glows with blue energy, disrupting the life force of living creatures you touch. Each touch deals 1d6 points of damage, plus 1 point of Strength damage unless the target succeeds on a Fortitude save. You can make one touch attack per caster level. An undead creature you touch takes no damage but must succeed on a Will save or flee as if panicked for 1d4 rounds + 1 round per caster level.

Circle of Death.description: You snuff out the life force of living creatures, killing them instantly. The spell slays 1d4 HD per caster level (maximum 20d4), affecting creatures with the fewest HD first, then closest first among equal HD. No creature of 9 or more HD can be affected. Insufficient remaining HD to affect a creature are wasted. Material Component: Powder from a crushed black pearl worth at least 500 gp.

Clairaudience/clairvoyance.description: You create an invisible sensor at a known location (familiar or obvious, such as behind a door or around a corner) that lets you hear or see (your choice) as if present. The sensor is stationary but can be rotated freely. Enhanced senses do not function through it. Magical darkness prevents seeing; natural pitch darkness allows vision in a 10-foot radius. This works only on your current plane. Arcane Focus: A small horn (for hearing) or a glass eye (for seeing).

Cloak of Chaos.description: A chaotic pattern of color surrounds the subjects, providing four effects: +4 deflection bonus to AC and +4 resistance bonus on saves against all attacks (not just from lawful creatures); spell resistance 25 against lawful spells and spells cast by lawful creatures; protection from possession and mental influence as protection from law; and any lawful creature that succeeds on a melee attack against a warded subject is confused for 1 round (Will negates). Focus: A tiny reliquary with a sacred relic from a chaotic text, costing at least 500 gp.

Clone.description: You create an inert duplicate of a creature. If the original dies, its soul instantly transfers to the clone, and the original's remains become permanently inert. Cloning fails if the original died of natural causes. You need a piece of living flesh (at least 1 cubic inch, not hair or nails) preserved from rotting. The clone must grow in a laboratory for 2d4 months. The clone is physically identical and shares the original's personality and memories, but treat it as if raised from the dead (losing one level or 2 Constitution points). If this would reduce Constitution to 0, the spell fails. If the original lost levels since the flesh was taken and died at a lower level, the clone is one level below the death level. Only body and mind are duplicated, not equipment. A clone grown while the original lives is merely inert flesh that rots without preservation. Material Component: The flesh and laboratory supplies (1,000 gp). Focus: Laboratory equipment (500 gp).

Cloudkill.description: You generate a bank of poisonous yellowish-green fog similar to fog cloud. Creatures with 3 or fewer HD are automatically killed (no save). Those with 4 to 6 HD die unless they succeed on a Fortitude save (taking 1d4 Constitution damage per round on failure). Creatures with 6+ HD take 1d4 Constitution damage per round (Fortitude halves). Holding one's breath does not help; poison-immune creatures are unaffected. The cloud moves away from you at 10 feet per round along the ground, sinking to the lowest available terrain. It cannot penetrate liquids or be cast underwater.

Color Spray.description: A vivid cone of clashing colors erupts from your hand, affecting creatures based on their HD. 2 HD or less: unconscious, blinded, and stunned for 2d4 rounds, then blinded and stunned for 1d4 rounds, then stunned for 1 round (only living creatures are knocked unconscious). 3 or 4 HD: blinded and stunned for 1d4 rounds, then stunned for 1 round. 5+ HD: stunned for 1 round. Sightless creatures are unaffected. Material Component: A pinch each of red, yellow, and blue powder or sand.

Command.description: You issue a single one-word command that the subject obeys as best it can on its next turn. Options include: Approach (moves toward you), Drop (drops held items), Fall (falls prone), Flee (moves away), and Halt (stands still taking no actions). If the subject cannot comply, the spell fails.

Command Plants.description: You exert influence over plant creatures. Affected subjects understand you, perceive your actions favorably, and will not attack you. Giving orders beyond normal behavior requires winning an opposed Charisma check (no retries). A commanded plant never obeys suicidal or obviously harmful orders. You can affect plant creatures whose combined HD do not exceed twice your level.

Command Undead.description: You gain influence over an undead creature. An intelligent undead perceives your actions favorably and will not attack you. Giving unusual orders requires an opposed Charisma check (no retries). Intelligent undead never obey suicidal orders. A mindless undead (skeleton, zombie) gets no saving throw and follows basic commands like come, go, fight, or stand still, including suicidal ones. Any threatening act by you or your allies ends the spell. Commands are not telepathic and must be audible. Material Component: Raw meat and a bone splinter.

Command, Greater.description: This functions like command, except you can affect up to one creature per level, the activity continues beyond 1 round, and each creature gets a new Will save at the start of its turn after the first. All creatures must receive the same command.

Commune.description: You contact your deity or its agents and ask yes-or-no questions, one per caster level. Answers are correct within the entity's knowledge. "Unclear" is valid since powerful beings are not omniscient. Short phrases may replace one-word answers when necessary to avoid misleading. The entities structure answers to further their own purposes. The spell ends if you stop to discuss answers or take other actions. Material Component: Holy (or unholy) water and incense. XP Cost: 100 XP.

Commune With Nature.description: You attune yourself to the surrounding territory, gaining immediate knowledge of up to three facts about: terrain, plants, minerals, water sources, people, general animal population, woodland creatures, powerful unnatural creatures, or the general state of nature. Outdoors, the radius is 1 mile per caster level; underground, it is 100 feet per caster level. The spell does not work in areas where nature has been replaced by construction or settlement.

Comprehend Languages.description: You gain the ability to understand spoken words or read otherwise incomprehensible text by touching the creature or writing. You can read one page (250 words) per minute. This grants literal understanding only, not insight. It does not allow you to speak or write the language. Magical writing cannot be read (though it is revealed as magical). The spell does not decipher codes or uncover hidden messages within normal text. It can be made permanent with permanency. Arcane Material Component: A pinch of soot and a few grains of salt.

Cone of Cold.description: You create an area of extreme cold extending outward from your hand in a cone, draining heat and dealing 1d6 points of cold damage per caster level (maximum 15d6). Arcane Material Component: A very small crystal or glass cone.

Confusion.description: Targets become unable to independently determine their actions. Each round, a random roll determines what an affected creature does. A confused creature that cannot perform the indicated action babbles incoherently. Attackers gain no special advantage against confused targets. A confused creature that is attacked automatically retaliates on its next turn while still confused. Arcane Material Component: Three nut shells.

Confusion, Lesser.description: You cause a single creature to become confused for 1 round, with effects as the confusion spell.

Consecrate.description: You bless an area with positive energy. Turning checks within the area gain a +3 sacred bonus. Undead entering the area suffer a -1 penalty on attack rolls, damage rolls, and saves. Undead cannot be created or summoned within the area. If the area contains a permanent fixture dedicated to your deity, all modifiers double. A fixture of another deity is instead cursed, severing its divine connection (without the undead-related benefits). This spell counters and dispels desecrate. Material Component: A vial of holy water and 25 gp worth of silver dust.

Contact Other Plane.description: You project your mind to another plane to seek advice from extraplanar powers. They respond with brief one-word answers. You ask one question per two caster levels, requiring concentration (standard action) each round. Contacting more distant planes increases both the risk of Intelligence and Charisma loss and the likelihood of receiving accurate answers. Results may be modified by the GM based on the personalities of specific deities. Rarely, this divination may be blocked by certain powers.

Contagion.description: The target contracts a disease of your choice, which takes effect immediately with no incubation period.

Contingency.description: You place a companion spell upon yourself that triggers under conditions you specify. Both spells are cast simultaneously during the 10-minute minimum casting time. The companion spell must affect your person and be no higher than one-third your caster level (maximum 6th level). Conditions must be clear, though they can be general. The companion spell activates instantaneously when conditions are met, regardless of your wishes. Overly complicated conditions may cause the combination to fail. Only one contingency can be active at a time. Material Component: Companion spell components plus quicksilver and an eyelash from a spell-using creature. Focus: An ivory statuette of yourself decorated with gems (worth at least 1,500 gp), which you must carry.

Continual Flame.description: A torch-bright flame springs from an object you touch. It looks like a real flame but produces no heat and consumes no oxygen. It can be covered or hidden but not smothered or quenched. Light spells counter and dispel darkness spells of equal or lower level. Material Component: Ruby dust worth 50 gp.

Control Plants.description: You command plant creatures by voice for a short period. They understand you regardless of language. Even if silenced, controlled plants will not attack you. At the spell's end, they revert to normal behavior. Suicidal or self-destructive commands are ignored.

Control Undead.description: You command undead creatures by voice for a short period. They understand you regardless of language. Even if silenced, controlled undead will not attack you. At the spell's end, they revert to normal behavior. Intelligent undead remember being controlled. Material Component: A piece of bone and a piece of raw meat.

Control Water.description: You raise or lower water. Lower Water reduces depth by up to 2 feet per caster level (minimum 1 inch) in an area up to caster level x 10 feet per side. In deep water, this creates a whirlpool trapping ships. When used on water elementals and water-based creatures, it acts as a slow spell (Will negates). Raise Water increases water height correspondingly and may spill onto nearby land. You may halve one horizontal dimension and double the other. Arcane Material Component: A drop of water (raise) or pinch of dust (lower).

Control Weather.description: You change local weather over 10 minutes of casting plus 10 minutes for effects to manifest. You can call weather appropriate to the climate and season, controlling general tendencies like wind direction and intensity, but not specific effects like individual lightning strikes. New weather manifests gradually over 10 minutes. You can change weather types with a standard action (also manifesting in 10 minutes). Contradictory conditions cannot coexist. A druid doubles the duration and affects a 3-mile radius circle.

Control Winds.description: You alter wind force in the surrounding area, adjusting direction, strength, or both. Changes persist until the spell ends or you alter them (requiring concentration). You may create an "eye" of calm up to 80 feet in diameter at the center. Wind Direction: You may choose from four basic wind patterns over the spell's area.

Create Food and Water.description: You create simple, nourishing food of your choice (bland but wholesome). It decays within 24 hours unless preserved by purify food and water for another 24 hours. The water is equivalent to clean rain water and does not spoil.

Create Greater Undead.description: This functions like create undead, except you can create more powerful undead types: shadows, wraiths, spectres, and devourers. The available type depends on your caster level.

Create Undead.description: More powerful than animate dead, this spell creates intelligent undead: ghouls, ghasts, mummies, and mohrgs. The type depends on your caster level, and you may create weaker types than allowed. Created undead are not automatically under your control; you may attempt to command them as they form if you have that ability. The spell must be cast at night. Material Component: A clay pot of grave dirt, one of brackish water, and a black onyx gem worth at least 50 gp per HD, placed in each corpse. The gems are consumed.

Create Water.description: You generate clean, drinkable water in a container as small as needed or up to three times as large, potentially filling many receptacles. Water weighs about 8 pounds per gallon; one cubic foot contains roughly 8 gallons and weighs about 60 pounds.

Creeping Doom.description: You summon a mass of centipede swarms (one per two caster levels, maximum ten at 20th level) that need not appear adjacent. They attack any creatures in their area and remain stationary unless you direct them (standard action). You can command any number of swarms to pursue prey within 100 feet. Swarms that move beyond 100 feet become stationary but can be commanded again if you return within range.

Crushing Despair.description: An invisible cone of despair afflicts subjects with a -2 penalty on attack rolls, saving throws, ability checks, skill checks, and weapon damage rolls. This spell counters and dispels good hope. Material Component: A vial of tears.

Cure Critical Wounds.description: This functions like cure light wounds, except it restores 4d8 points of damage + 1 per caster level (maximum +20).

Cure Critical Wounds, Mass.description: This functions like mass cure light wounds, except it restores 4d8 points of damage + 1 per caster level (maximum +40).

Cure Light Wounds.description: By laying your hand on a living creature, you channel positive energy to heal 1d8 points of damage + 1 per caster level (maximum +5). Against undead, this spell deals damage instead. An undead creature can apply spell resistance and attempt a Will save for half damage.

Cure Light Wounds, Mass.description: You channel positive energy to heal 1d8 points of damage + 1 per caster level (maximum +25) to each selected creature. Undead in the area take damage instead and may attempt Will saves for half.

Cure Minor Wounds.description: This functions like cure light wounds, except it heals only 1 point of damage.

Cure Moderate Wounds.description: This functions like cure light wounds, except it restores 2d8 points of damage + 1 per caster level (maximum +10).

Cure Moderate Wounds, Mass.description: This functions like mass cure light wounds, except it restores 2d8 points of damage + 1 per caster level (maximum +30).

Cure Serious Wounds.description: This functions like cure light wounds, except it restores 3d8 points of damage + 1 per caster level (maximum +15).

Cure Serious Wounds, Mass.description: This functions like mass cure light wounds, except it restores 3d8 points of damage + 1 per caster level (maximum +35).

Curse Water.description: You imbue a flask (1 pint) of water with negative energy, creating unholy water. Unholy water damages good outsiders in the same way holy water damages undead and evil outsiders. Material Component: 5 pounds of powdered silver (worth 25 gp).

Dancing Lights.description: You create up to four lights resembling lanterns or torches (casting equivalent illumination), up to four glowing spheres, or one faintly glowing humanoid shape. The lights must remain within a 10-foot radius of each other but move as you desire without concentration, up to 100 feet per round. A light winks out if it exceeds the spell's range. This spell can be made permanent with permanency.

Darkness.description: An object you target radiates shadowy illumination in a 20-foot radius, granting all creatures within 20% concealment. Even darkvision and low-light vision do not negate this miss chance. Normal light sources cannot brighten the area, nor can lower-level light spells. Higher-level light spells are unaffected. If cast on a small object placed under lightproof covering, the effect is blocked until uncovered. Darkness counters or dispels equal or lower level light spells. Arcane Material Component: A bit of bat fur and a drop of pitch or piece of coal.

Darkvision.description: The subject gains 60-foot darkvision (black-and-white vision in total darkness). This does not function in magical darkness. It can be made permanent with permanency. Material Component: A pinch of dried carrot or an agate.

Daylight.description: The touched object sheds bright light in a 60-foot radius and dim light for another 60 feet beyond that. Creatures sensitive to bright light suffer penalties within the radius. Despite its name, this is not equivalent to actual sunlight for creatures damaged by it. If cast on a small object under lightproof covering, the effect is blocked until uncovered. Daylight and magical darkness temporarily negate each other in overlapping areas. This counters or dispels darkness spells of equal or lower level.

Daze.description: You cloud the mind of a humanoid creature with 4 or fewer HD, causing it to take no actions. Humanoids of 5+ HD are unaffected. A dazed creature is not stunned, so attackers gain no special advantage. Material Component: A pinch of wool or similar substance.

Daze Monster.description: This functions like daze, except it can affect any living creature of any type. Creatures of 7+ HD are unaffected.

Death Knell.description: You draw the fading life force from a creature with -1 or fewer hit points that you touch. On a failed save, it dies, and you gain 1d8 temporary hit points, +2 Strength, and +1 effective caster level (not granting access to higher-level spells). These benefits last 10 minutes per HD of the slain creature.

Death Ward.description: The target becomes immune to all death spells, magical death effects, energy drain, and negative energy effects (such as inflict spells or chill touch). This does not remove existing negative levels or affect the 24-hour save against them. It does not protect against hit point loss, poison, petrification, or other potentially lethal non-death effects.

Deathwatch.description: Using the sight of unlife, you instantly determine the condition of nearby creatures: dead, fragile (alive with 3 or fewer hp), fighting off death (alive with 4+ hp), undead, or neither alive nor dead (such as a construct). This sight penetrates abilities that allow creatures to feign death.

Deep Slumber.description: This functions like sleep, except it affects 10 HD of creatures.

Deeper Darkness.description: This functions like darkness, except the shadowy illumination extends to a 60-foot radius and lasts longer. Daylight and deeper darkness temporarily negate each other in overlapping areas. This counters and dispels light spells of equal or lower level, including daylight and light.

Delay Poison.description: The target becomes temporarily immune to poison. Any poison in its system or encountered during the spell's duration has no effect until the spell expires. This does not cure damage already inflicted by poison.

Delayed Blast Fireball.description: This functions like fireball, except it deals 1d6 fire damage per caster level (maximum 20d6) and can be delayed up to 5 rounds after casting. The glowing bead sits at its destination until detonation. A creature can pick up and throw the bead (10-foot range increment). If handled within 1 round of detonation, there is a 25% chance of premature detonation.

Demand.description: This functions like sending, but the message can include a suggestion effect. A successful Will save negates the suggestion but not the contact itself. The demand is understood even by creatures with Intelligence as low as 1. Impossible or meaningless messages are understood but the suggestion has no effect. The message including the suggestion must be 25 words or less. Material Component: Copper wire and a small part of the subject.

Desecrate.description: You imbue an area with negative energy. Turning checks take a -3 profane penalty, and undead in the area gain +1 profane bonus on attack rolls, damage rolls, and saves. Undead created or summoned in the area gain +1 hp per HD. If the area contains a fixture dedicated to your deity, all modifiers double, and animate dead can create double the normal amount. A fixture of another deity is instead cursed. This spell counters and dispels consecrate. Material Component: A vial of unholy water and 25 gp worth of silver dust.

Destruction.description: The target is instantly slain and its remains utterly consumed (equipment is unaffected). A successful Fortitude save instead deals 10d6 points of damage. Only true resurrection, a carefully worded wish followed by resurrection, or miracle can restore a creature killed by this spell. Focus: A special silver holy (or unholy) symbol marked with verses of anathema (500 gp).

Detect Animals Or Plants.description: You detect a specific kind of animal or plant in a cone. You can change the target kind each round. 1st Round: Presence or absence. 2nd Round: Number and condition of the healthiest. 3rd Round: Condition and location of each. Conditions are Normal (90%+ hp), Fair (30-90%), Poor (below 30% or diseased), and Weak (0 or fewer hp, terminal disease, or crippled). The spell penetrates barriers except 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of metal, thin lead, or 3 feet of wood/dirt.

Detect Chaos.description: This functions like detect evil, except it detects chaotic auras from creatures, clerics, spells, and magic items. Lawful creatures are vulnerable to overwhelming chaotic auras.

Detect Evil.description: You sense evil presence in a cone. 1st Round: Presence or absence. 2nd Round: Number and power of evil auras; good characters may be stunned by overwhelming evil auras from sources with HD at least twice their level. 3rd Round: Power and location of each aura. Aura strength depends on the source's type, HD, caster level, or class level. Lingering auras persist as dim after the source dissipates. Animals, traps, and poisons are not evil. The spell penetrates barriers except 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of metal, thin lead, or 3 feet of wood/dirt.

Detect Good.description: This functions like detect evil, except it detects good auras. Evil creatures are vulnerable to overwhelming good auras. Healing potions and similar beneficial items do not register as good.

Detect Law.description: This functions like detect evil, except it detects lawful auras. Chaotic creatures are vulnerable to overwhelming lawful auras.

Detect Magic.description: You sense magical auras in a cone. 1st Round: Presence or absence. 2nd Round: Number and strength of the strongest aura. 3rd Round: Strength and location of each aura. With line of sight, Spellcraft checks (DC 15 + spell level, or 15 + half caster level for non-spell effects) identify the school. Strong local emanations may distort weaker auras. Lingering auras persist as dim after the source is gone. Summoned outsiders and elementals register their conjuration spell. The spell penetrates barriers except 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of metal, thin lead, or 3 feet of wood/dirt. It can be made permanent with permanency.

Detect Poison.description: You determine whether a creature, object, or area is poisoned or poisonous. The exact type can be identified with a DC 20 Wisdom check or DC 20 Craft (alchemy) check. The spell penetrates barriers except 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of metal, thin lead, or 3 feet of wood/dirt.

Detect Scrying.description: You immediately become aware of any divination (scrying) attempt to observe you within the spell's area. You know the location of every magical sensor. If the scrying originates within the area, you know its location; otherwise, you and the scrier make opposed caster level checks. If you match or exceed the scrier's result, you gain a visual image and accurate sense of direction and distance. Material Component: A piece of mirror and a miniature brass hearing trumpet.

Detect Secret Doors.description: You detect doors, compartments, and caches specifically constructed to escape detection. 1st Round: Presence or absence. 2nd Round: Number and location (direction if not in line of sight). Additional Rounds: The mechanism or trigger for one closely examined portal per round. The spell penetrates barriers except 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of metal, thin lead, or 3 feet of wood/dirt.

Detect Snares and Pits.description: You detect simple pits, deadfalls, snares, and mechanical traps of natural materials, plus natural hazards like quicksand, sinkholes, and unstable rock walls. It does not detect complex traps, magic traps (except pit/deadfall/snare types), inactive traps, or non-trap hazards. 1st Round: Presence. 2nd Round: Number and location. Additional Rounds: Type and trigger per hazard examined. Penetrates barriers except 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of metal, thin lead, or 3 feet of wood/dirt.

Detect Thoughts.description: You sense surface thoughts in a cone. 1st Round: Presence of conscious minds (Intelligence 1+). 2nd Round: Number and Intelligence of each; if the highest is 26+ and 10+ points above yours, you are stunned for 1 round. 3rd Round: Surface thoughts of any mind; a Will save blocks reading. Animal minds produce simple instinctual thoughts. The spell penetrates barriers except 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of metal, thin lead, or 3 feet of wood/dirt. Arcane Focus: A copper piece.

Detect Undead.description: You detect undead auras in a cone. 1st Round: Presence. 2nd Round: Number and strength of the strongest; good characters may be stunned by overwhelming auras from undead with HD at least twice their level. 3rd Round: Strength and location of each. Lingering auras persist as dim. The spell penetrates barriers except 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of metal, thin lead, or 3 feet of wood/dirt. Arcane Material Component: A bit of grave earth.

Dictum.description: Any nonlawful creature in the area suffers cumulative effects with no save based on HD relative to your caster level: deafened 1d4 rounds, slowed 2d4 rounds, paralyzed 1d10 minutes, and killed (living creatures die, undead are destroyed). Nonlawful extraplanar creatures on your home plane are banished for at least 24 hours (Will at -4 negates). Creatures with HD exceeding your caster level are unaffected.

Dimension Door.description: You instantly teleport to any spot within range by visualizing it or stating direction and distance. You cannot take other actions until your next turn. You can bring objects up to your maximum load and one additional willing Medium or smaller creature per three caster levels (Large counts as two Medium, etc.). All must be touching. Arriving in a solid object deals 1d6 damage and shunts you to a random open space within 100 feet; if none, additional 2d6 damage and shunted within 1,000 feet; if still none, additional 4d6 and the spell fails.

Dimensional Anchor.description: A green ray (requiring a ranged touch attack) covers the target with a shimmering emerald field that completely blocks extradimensional travel including astral projection, blink, dimension door, ethereal jaunt, gate, maze, plane shift, shadow walk, teleport, and similar abilities. It also prevents use of gates and teleportation circles. It does not interfere with already-ethereal or astral creatures, extradimensional perception or attacks, or summoned creatures disappearing at spell end.

Dimensional Lock.description: You create a shimmering emerald barrier that completely blocks extradimensional travel into or out of the area, including astral projection, blink, dimension door, ethereal jaunt, gate, maze, plane shift, shadow walk, teleport, and similar abilities. It does not affect already-ethereal/astral creatures, extradimensional perception or attacks, or summoned creatures disappearing at spell end.

Diminish Plants.description: Two versions available. Prune Growth: Normal vegetation within long range shrinks to about one-third size, becoming untangled and neatly trimmed. You select the area shape and may designate unaffected portions. Stunt Growth: Normal plants within half a mile have their productivity reduced by one-third over the following year. This counters plant growth and does not affect plant creatures.

Discern Lies.description: Each round, you concentrate on one subject within range. You detect deliberate, knowing lies by perceiving disturbances in the subject's aura. The spell does not reveal truth, unintentional inaccuracies, or evasions. You may switch subjects each round.

Discern Location.description: One of the most powerful locating spells available. Nothing short of mind blank or direct divine intervention prevents you from learning the exact location of a single creature or object. The spell reveals the name, community, political division, country, continent, and plane of existence. You must have seen the creature or touched the object at least once.

Disguise Self.description: You alter your appearance including clothing, armor, weapons, and equipment. You can appear up to 1 foot shorter or taller, thinner, heavier, or in between, but cannot change your body type. The spell provides no new abilities, mannerisms, or altered tactile/audible properties. Equipment appears different but functions normally. This grants a +10 bonus on Disguise checks. Creatures that interact with the illusion get a Will save to recognize it.

Disintegrate.description: A thin green ray springs from your finger (requiring a ranged touch attack), dealing 2d6 damage per caster level (maximum 40d6). A creature reduced to 0 or fewer hp is entirely disintegrated, leaving only fine dust; equipment is unaffected. Against objects, it disintegrates up to one 10-foot cube of nonliving matter. It affects force constructs but not globes of invulnerability or antimagic fields. A successful Fortitude save reduces damage to 5d6; if this reduces the target to 0 hp, it is still disintegrated. Only the first target struck is affected. Arcane Material Component: A lodestone and a pinch of dust.

Dismissal.description: You force an extraplanar creature back to its home plane on a failed special Will save (DC = spell's save DC - creature's HD + your caster level). Success sends the creature away, though there is a 20% chance it arrives on a plane other than its own.

Dispel Chaos.description: This functions like dispel evil, except you are surrounded by constant, blue lawful energy, and it affects chaotic creatures and spells.

Dispel Evil.description: Shimmering white holy energy surrounds you with three effects. First, you gain a +4 deflection bonus to AC against evil creatures. Second, a successful melee touch attack against an evil extraplanar creature can drive it to its home plane (Will negates; this discharges the spell). Third, a touch automatically dispels one enchantment from an evil caster or one evil spell (except those immune to dispel magic; no save or spell resistance; this discharges the spell).

Dispel Good.description: This functions like dispel evil, except you are surrounded by dark, wavering unholy energy, and it affects good creatures and spells.

Dispel Law.description: This functions like dispel evil, except you are surrounded by flickering yellow chaotic energy, and it affects lawful creatures and spells.

Dispel Magic.description: You can end ongoing spells on a creature or object, suppress magic items, counter spells, or dispel effects in an area. A dispelled spell ends as if its duration expired. Instantaneous effects cannot be dispelled. Three modes are available. Targeted Dispel: Make a dispel check (1d20 + caster level, maximum +10) against DC 11 + each effect's caster level. Success on magic items suppresses them for 1d4 rounds. Artifacts and deities are unaffected. You automatically succeed against your own spells. Area Dispel: Affects everything in a 20-foot radius. For each creature, check against the highest caster level spell first, then progressively weaker ones until one is dispelled or all checks fail. Magic items in the area are not affected. Counterspell: Target a spellcaster and make a dispel check to counter their spell.

Dispel Magic, Greater.description: This functions like dispel magic, except the maximum caster level bonus on your dispel check is +20 instead of +10, and it has a chance to dispel effects that remove curse can remove even if normal dispel magic cannot.

Displacement.description: The target appears to be about 2 feet from its actual location, granting a 50% miss chance as if it had total concealment. Unlike actual total concealment, enemies can still target the creature normally. True seeing reveals the true location. Material Component: A small twisted loop of leather from a displacer beast hide.

Disrupt Undead.description: You fire a ray of positive energy. A successful ranged touch attack against an undead creature deals 1d6 damage.

Disrupting Weapon.description: A melee weapon becomes deadly to undead. Any undead with HD equal to or less than your caster level struck by the weapon must succeed on a Will save or be utterly destroyed. Spell resistance does not apply to the destruction effect.

Divination.description: More powerful than augury, this provides useful advice about a specific goal, event, or activity within one week. The advice may be a short phrase or cryptic omen. The base chance for accuracy is 70% + 1% per caster level (maximum 90%). A failed roll is known unless false information magic is at work. Repeated divinations on the same topic by the same caster yield the same result. Material Component: Incense and a sacrificial offering worth at least 25 gp.

Divine Favor.description: Drawing upon divine strength, you gain a +1 luck bonus on attack and weapon damage rolls for every three caster levels (minimum +1, maximum +3). This does not apply to spell damage.

Divine Power.description: You imbue yourself with divine might. Your base attack bonus equals your character level (potentially granting extra attacks), you gain a +6 enhancement bonus to Strength, and you gain 1 temporary hit point per caster level.

Dominate Animal.description: You enchant an animal, directing it with simple commands. Suicidal orders or commands to attack creatures two or more size categories larger are ignored. A mental link allows silent commands while in range without needing to see the creature. You know what it experiences but receive no direct sensory input. Its actions may exceed its normal comprehension since you provide the intelligence. Changing commands is a move action.

Dominate Monster.description: This functions like dominate person, except it is not restricted by creature type.

Dominate Person.description: You control a humanoid through a telepathic link. With a common language, you can force most actions within its abilities; without, only basic commands. You know what the subject experiences. It continues carrying out commands to the exclusion of other activities (a DC 15 Sense Motive check can detect the influence). Changing commands is a move action. Full concentration (standard action) grants full sensory input through the subject's mind. Subjects forced against their nature get a new save at +2. Self-destructive orders are not carried out. Range is unlimited on the same plane once established. Without daily concentration, the subject gets a new save. Protection from evil blocks control but does not end or prevent domination.

Doom.description: You fill the target with horrible dread, causing it to become shaken.

Drawmij's Instant Summons.description: You call a nonliving item to your hand from virtually any location. First, place your arcane mark on the item, then cast this spell to inscribe the item's name on a sapphire (worth at least 1,000 gp). Thereafter, speaking a command word and crushing the gem summons the item instantly. If another creature possesses it, the spell fails but reveals the possessor's identity and approximate location. The item can be summoned across planes unless another creature has claimed it. Material Component: A sapphire worth at least 1,000 gp.

Dream.description: You or a touched messenger sends a phantasmal message to a named recipient through their dreams. The message can be any length and is perfectly remembered. Communication is one-way. The messenger enters a trance and appears in the recipient's dream. If the recipient is awake, the messenger can wait in the trance until the recipient sleeps. A disturbed messenger wakes, ending the spell. Creatures that do not sleep or dream cannot be contacted. The messenger is defenseless during the trance.

Eagle's Splendor.description: The target becomes more poised and personally forceful, gaining a +4 enhancement bonus to Charisma. Charisma-based spellcasters gain increased save DCs but not extra spell slots. Arcane Material Component: A few eagle feathers or a pinch of eagle droppings.

Eagle's Splendor, Mass.description: This functions like eagle's splendor, except it affects multiple creatures.

Earthquake.description: An intense, localized tremor rips the ground for 1 round. Creatures on the ground cannot move or attack. Spellcasters must make a Concentration check (DC 20 + spell level) or lose spells. Effects vary by terrain: Cave/Tunnel: Roof collapses for 8d6 bludgeoning (Reflex DC 15 half), pinning creatures. Cliff: Creates a landslide traveling horizontally equal to the fall distance, dealing 8d6 (Reflex DC 15 half) and pinning. Open Ground: DC 15 Reflex or fall prone; 25% chance of falling into a fissure (Reflex DC 20 to avoid); fissures close at spell's end, killing trapped creatures. Structure: 100 points of damage (ignoring hardness), collapsing typical buildings; trapped creatures take 8d6 (Reflex DC 15 half). River/Lake/Marsh: Fissures drain water; swampland becomes quicksand (DC 15 Reflex or sink). Pinned creatures take 1d6 nonlethal per minute; unconscious pinned creatures must make DC 15 Constitution checks or take 1d6 lethal per minute.

Elemental Swarm.description: You open a portal to an Elemental Plane and summon elementals. First, 2d4 Large elementals appear. Ten minutes later, 1d4 Huge elementals arrive. Ten minutes after that, one greater elemental appears. All have maximum hit points and serve you for the duration, obeying explicitly. No concentration is needed. You can dismiss them individually or as groups. The spell takes on the type descriptor matching the summoned element.

Endure Elements.description: The protected creature suffers no harm from temperatures between -50 and 140 degrees Fahrenheit without Fortitude saves. Equipment is also protected. This provides no protection from fire or cold damage or other environmental hazards like smoke or lack of air.

Energy Drain.description: This functions like enervation, except the target gains 2d4 negative levels that last longer. No saving throw prevents gaining the levels, but 24 hours later, the subject makes a Fortitude save for each level; success removes the negative level, while failure also removes it but permanently drains one character level. An undead creature struck gains 2d4 x 5 temporary hit points for 1 hour.

Enervation.description: A black ray of negative energy (requiring a ranged touch attack) inflicts 1d4 negative levels on the target. A creature with negative levels equal to or exceeding its HD dies. Each negative level imposes -1 on attack rolls, saves, skill checks, ability checks, and effective level, plus costs one highest-level spell slot. Lost levels are regained after a number of hours equal to your caster level (maximum 15). Unlike normal negative levels, these do not risk permanent drain. An undead target gains 1d4 x 5 temporary hit points for 1 hour.

Enlarge Person.description: A humanoid instantly doubles in height and multiplies its weight by 8, advancing one size category.
